proved: For centered iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2] original coordinates, every rank-r orthogonal projection for r=1 or 2 has a strictly positive density lower bound on the radius-1/4 ball, uniformly over the projection orientation for that fixed ambient dimension.
Every nonzero rank-one symmetric matrix admits a cap-one product input whose quadratic output density has an inverse-square-root blow-up.
Every rank-two indefinite symmetric matrix, in every orientation, admits a cap-one product input whose quadratic output density has a logarithmic blow-up.

Every rank-two semidefinite symmetric matrix has a bounded density for every cap-one product input, with height at most 2*pi/sqrt(|lambda1 lambda2|), but there is a cap-one product input for which no continuous density representative exists.
Together with the completed fixed-matrix rank>=3 theorem, rank three is the exact qualitative threshold for: every cap-one product law gives a bounded C0 quadratic density.

For a disjoint-bank target with a rank-two semidefinite bank carrying two large eigenvalues and an independent bank carrying a third large eigenvalue, height is at most 2*pi; account04/B15 r8 upgrades the paid interval bound to C0 with the same constant.
